notes: After spending 5 on Carmen T1 and 5 more breaking Doomscroll T4 to hit a Behold! trap, the Runner sat broke for turns 5-11, paying 2 credits a click to remove Behold!/Witch Hunt tags one at a time (T5, T6, T8, T9, T10, T11) and clicking for credits. Meanwhile the Corp advanced Server 3 over T6-T9 (Tomorrow's Headline, Witch Hunt) with no pressure; the T7 Tread Lightly and T11 runs into unrezzed Ping were made with 0-1 credits.

Sericulture Expansion went to an open Archives (stolen T6), and Hybrid Release was installed twice in Server 3 behind a lone Diviner that Utae had already broken on T5 (stolen T7 and T11). Rezzing Ivik for 6 on T6 left the Corp at 0-2 credits from T7 on, unable to rez its R&D ice, and Fujii Asset Retrieval was taken from R&D T11; the T4/T7/T8 credit clicks also ended in hand-size discards.

The Runner spent turns 2-9 and again 21-27 doing nothing but clicking for credits, banking up to 36 credits while never running R&D or HQ. On T19 it clicked for credits instead of contesting Server 2, and the Corp scored Oracle Thinktank there T20; the win came only because the Corp installed Artificial Cryptocrash naked on T28.

Scoring Project Yagi-Uda T2 and two Sericulture Expansions in Server 1 worked, but the Corp sat at 0-3 credits all game and never rezzed its R&D ice. The Runner got about 20 free R&D accesses and stole Fujii T8; HQ was also left open T1-T2, and the T11 discard came while clicking for credits.

Turn 1 spent everything on Carmen, then facechecked R&D (Jailbreak) and HQ (Concerto) with 0 credits. From T4 to T12 the Runner ran into the already-rezzed N-Pot on HQ and Ping on R&D over a dozen times with no means to break them, wasting nearly every turn. The win only came later via Tremolo plus bad-publicity credits on R&D.

Sericulture Expansion was installed in Server 2 while the Corp had too few credits to rez both ice (stolen T3), and Hybrid Release was put there again on T4 with 2 credits (stolen). The game-losing error came on T5: after Hedge Fund and Cultivate, the Corp discarded 2 cards (Project Yagi-Uda and Sericulture) into an unprotected Archives and spent T6 icing Server 2 instead, and the Runner took both from Archives for the win.

Good remote pressure stole Remastered Edition T4 and Oracle Thinktank T5, and R&D pressure later won the game. Tag handling was sloppy, though: it kept running through Vasilisa on R&D every turn (T6-T12) and stayed tagged with resources out, so the Corp trashed Daily Casts repeatedly, and it paid 6 to Grubber on T8 to see a Tiered Subscription.

The Runner never installed a breaker and spent turns 4-7, 9-13, 16, 18 and 20-21 clicking for credits, banking 58 credits it never used. It let Remastered Edition (T9-10), Artificial Cryptocrash (T19-20) and Next Big Thing (advanced T21-22) score from remotes uncontested, and its only remote runs (T8, T19) facechecked unrezzed ETR ice with no breakers.

The Corp spent 5 to rez Saisentan on T4 protecting a Mavirus trap, leaving 0 credits, so the HQ ice stayed unrezzed and Hybrid Release was taken from HQ T5. On T10 it scored Longevity Serum and trashed its whole 5-card hand, putting Lotus Haze and See How They Run into an unprotected Archives that the Runner ran immediately for the win.

Turn 1 left R&D and HQ unprotected, and the Runner stole three agendas from R&D; after that the Corp cleanly scored Longevity Serum T4 and See How They Run T5 from remotes. Economy was thin (0-3 credits for most of the game), but Sisyphus Protocol and Lotus Haze were scored from a 2-ice Server 2 for the win.

Three Hybrid Releases were installed naked in new remotes (T1, T3, T4) and scored the next turn, which only worked because the Runner never checked them. Spending 5 on Knowledge Seeker T7 left the Corp at 0-1 credits for the rest of the game with the R&D ice never rezzed, but Lotus Haze and See How They Run were scored from Server 5.

Telework Contract and Daily Casts built a solid economy, paying through Grubber to steal Artificial Cryptocrash T5 was good, and Nanuq through Capacitor took Next Big Thing for the win. Mistakes were small: the T4 R&D run into known Paywall with 1 credit and the T6 Server 1 run that paid 3 to Grubber and then let the run end, after which Oracle Thinktank scored T7.

See How They Run was installed and advanced behind a single Knowledge Seeker on T3 and stolen at once. The T5 Mitosis was odd, placing ice in two empty new remotes, and from T7 the Corp sat at 0-3 credits with only Hafrun on HQ (Lotus Haze stolen from HQ T10). It still won by grinding Hybrid Release, Longevity Serum, See How They Run and Sisyphus Protocol through Server 1.

With 10-14 credits on T8, the Runner clicked for credits instead of running Server 2 (one Ping) while the second Tomorrow's Headline was advanced and scored T9. Repeated tag clearing (T4, T11, T12, T14, T16) ate its tempo; at 6 points needing one steal, it idled on credits T17-T21 (up to 19 credits), and the Corp won with Flood the Market on the card installed T21.

Stealing Witch Hunt from Server 1 T2 and running R&D through unrezzed ice paid off. But turns 4-11 included a run into the known N-Pot on HQ almost every turn (T4, T5 with Tread Lightly, T6, T7, T8, T9, T11) when the Runner never had the 4 credits Sang Kancil needed. The economy stayed at 0-3 credits until Sure Gamble T11, and the win came from Jailbreak/Docklands Pass on HQ.

Flower Sermon was installed and advanced behind just Tatu-Bola on T2 and left unscored through T3 (stolen T3). HQ held Project Yagi-Uda and Sericulture Expansion behind ice that never got rezzed, and both were stolen T4-T5; Neurospike on T4 was played for no effect, and the Corp never had more than 5 credits.

Steals came steadily (Kingmaking T7, Artificial Cryptocrash T10 and T12, Oracle Thinktank T13), but the Runner kept running through Vasilisa and installing resources while tagged. That let the Corp trash Dr. Nuka Vrolyck T4, Daily Casts T5 and Daeg T8, and score Backroom Machinations off a tag T4; it also ran into unrezzed Capacitor on T9 while tagged.

On T4, T5 and T8 the Corp clicked for credits and then discarded 2, 3 and 2 cards to hand size, sending Flower Sermon and Sericulture Expansion into an Archives that was never iced; the Runner took both T9 for the win. Hybrid Release (T3) and Fujii Asset Retrieval (T8) were also stolen from Server 1.

With 13-14 credits, the Corp left R&D without ice until T7 while the Runner ran it 3-4 times a turn. On T2-T3 it drew and clicked for credits, then discarded 3, sending Sericulture Expansion into an open Archives (stolen T5, and another T9). Flower Sermon went behind a single Diviner that Utae could already break (stolen T10).

Next Big Thing from R&D T1 and the later remote steals were good, but on T2-T3 the Runner made eight HQ runs with 0 credits, seeing the same Daily Quest and Hype Machine, while Remastered Edition scored. It ran R&D four times on each of T7 and T8 without stealing, which re-accesses the same top card, made a T6 Server 1 run that died at Paywall, and clicked for credits on T16-T17 while holding 12-20 credits.
